Title: Stand Up the Cluster and Find Everything on Disk
What the shift is: Classic ZooKeeper-era cluster is already up (ZK + three brokers). Confirm processes on zookeeper and each broker, distrust handoff paths, find live ZK dataDir and Kafka log.dirs from the processes, and read the controller from ZooKeeper /controller. Leave live topics alone. Later labs move to KRaft.
What it teaches: ZooKeeper as control plane. Broker-only processes. Process env vs handoff decoy. Controller via /controller znode.

Title: Open a Topic the Platform Way
What the shift is: KRaft cluster (no ZooKeeper). Create order.status to the QuickBite shape: partition count, a replica on every broker, retention window, and a write accepted only when enough copies are in sync. Do not change the topics already live. The ticket template can be wrong—use the platform note.
What it teaches: A production topic is a shape (partitions, RF, min.ISR, retention), not a name. First KRaft lab after ZooKeeper orientation.

Title: Trace a Produce From Client to Last Replica
What the shift is: Produce a keyed record into rider.dispatch and trace it: bootstrap the client used, which partition it hashed to, which broker led that partition, which followers replicated it, and the log end on each replica.
What it teaches: bootstrap → metadata → leader. Partition / replica / ISR. Mapping a record to a broker and a log directory.

Title: The Partition and Replica Map
What the shift is: Before any incident, study one topic as a diagram: partitions, leaders, followers, ISR, preferred leader, min.insync.replicas, unclean leader election. Predict what happens for three RF / min.ISR combinations when one broker dies.
What it teaches: RF vs ISR. min.ISR as the write gate. Preferred replica. Unclean election as a durability tradeoff—not a green-button fix.

Title: Under-Replicated Is Not a Failed Write
What the shift is: rider.dispatch still accepts produces, but UnderReplicatedPartitions is non-zero because one broker is down. Bring it back and wait until every partition has a full ISR. Do not run a leader election by hand. Do not lower min.ISR.
What it teaches: URP ≠ produce error. Restoring a replica is wait-for-ISR, not elect-a-leader.

Title: min.ISR Is Why Produces Fail
What the shift is: Produces to a topic are failing. RF was left too low for the min.ISR still in force, and one of the remaining brokers is down. A note says to set min.ISR=1 so the page goes green. Do not. Restore RF and the broker; leave the durability rule intact.
What it teaches: Durability is the fix. Dropping min.ISR makes the page green and the next crash lose data.

Title: Segments Retention and Why Disk Fills
What the shift is: One broker keeps leaving the ISR. Its log directory is full: a leftover debug topic with retention off, plus a production topic left on keep-forever. Free the disk the platform way. Leave the hot path topic alone unless the ticket says otherwise. Learn delete vs compact on the status changelog.
What it teaches: Segments and indexes on disk. retention.ms / retention.bytes. delete keeps history; compact keeps latest per key. You cannot un-delete what compaction removed.

Title: Capstone: Disk ISR and the Write Path
What the shift is: Some partitions reject writes and a consumer group is behind on those same partitions. The leader's disk is full. Free the disk or let a caught-up replica take over. Lag must drain by reading. Leave min.ISR alone; do not enable unclean election; do not reset offsets to latest.
What it teaches: Stacks 1.5–1.7. One incident can be disk + ISR + stuck consume. Ticket shortcuts are wrong.

Title: Meet the Consumer Group
What the shift is: Start the dispatch-desk group on rider.dispatch. Record members, assigned partitions, committed offsets, and lag. Let it catch up. Do not reset anything.
What it teaches: Group topology. Lag = end − committed. Stable / PreparingRebalance / Empty.

Title: One Partition Stuck the Desk
What the shift is: Lag is only on one partition. The member assigned there is wedged. Restart that instance. Lag has to fall because the consumer reads—not because the saved position jumps to the end.
What it teaches: A stuck member is not a slow cluster. Resetting to latest hides unread records.

Title: Put the Offsets Back
What the shift is: During the last page someone moved restaurant-alerts to latest. Records are still in the log. Put the group back to the offsets in the ticket, then start it. Do not use earliest.
What it teaches: Committed offsets are the read position. Latest skips backlog. Earliest replays days not asked for.

Title: The Group Never Stays Stable
What the shift is: The group flaps: one member blows max.poll.interval, rejoins, and kicks everyone else. Fix member health (or remove the bad instance per the ticket). Do not hide it by raising session timeout.
What it teaches: Rebalance storms. max.poll / session / heartbeat. Stability before lag math.

Title: Replay Ate the Request Path
What the shift is: A replay client id is saturating produce/fetch and the desk falls behind. Topic describe looks fine. Put a quota on that client id only (or free headroom per the ticket) without killing the replay unless allowed.
What it teaches: Multi-tenant client pressure. Quotas are the platform lever when describe says the topic is healthy.

Title: Broker Identity Is the PVC
What the shift is: Inspect a three-broker Kafka on Kubernetes. Trace each broker pod: namespace, node, PVC, listeners, and the bootstrap the shell should use. Delete one broker pod and wait until it returns with the same cluster id and data.
What it teaches: Broker identity is PVC + node id. Topics are not resubmitted when a pod dies.

Title: Clients Are Calling an Address Brokers Do Not Advertise
What the shift is: Brokers are Running. CLI inside the pod works. Apps outside fail. Fix advertised.listeners / bootstrap Service / external hostname per the ticket. Do not open every port.
What it teaches: Listeners vs advertised.listeners. Client address ≠ inter-broker address.

Title: Roll One Broker at a Time
What the shift is: Patch brokers one at a time. Produces must still succeed under min.ISR=2; wait for full ISR after each restart. Do not restart all three. Do not enable unclean election.
What it teaches: Rolling restart as procedure. Quorum and ISR held through the roll.

Title: StorageClass and the Broker That Never Joins
What the shift is: A new broker pod stays pending or comes up empty: wrong StorageClass, unbound PVC, or volume that lost meta.properties. Fix storage so the broker rejoins with durable identity.
What it teaches: On K8s the disk lesson is provisioning and identity, not only df.

Title: Bootstrap Namespace and Listener Drift
What the shift is: Compound: bootstrap points at the wrong namespace Service, the right namespace cannot provision volumes, and the external listener hostname is one revision behind. Fix all three so a produce from the ticket shell succeeds.
What it teaches: Namespace + storage + listener replace 'which qb-broker script'.

Title: Topic Shape as Desired State
What the shift is: A desired-state file describes partitions, RF, min.ISR, and retention. Apply it so the sandbox matches. A second apply with no diff changes nothing.
What it teaches: Topic-as-code. Apply is idempotent.

Title: ACL and Quota From the Request File
What the shift is: A team request asks for produce on order.status and a produce quota. Finish the provisioner so it applies both from the request and leaves a receipt. Do not hand-edit one-off ACLs.
What it teaches: Access and quota are provisioned together. Receipt is the handoff.

Title: Refuse RF=1 and Keep-Forever
What the shift is: The same checker is handed RF=1 and retention forever (or a partition count over budget). It must refuse and leave the cluster unchanged.
What it teaches: Fail closed. Bad requests create nothing.

Title: Print Drift Then Repair
What the shift is: Desired file says rider.dispatch is RF=3 / min.ISR=2. Cluster was left at RF=2. First print the diff only. Then reconcile and wait until every partition is in sync.
What it teaches: Seeing drift and fixing drift are separate steps.

Title: Topic Request API
What the shift is: A small local API other teams call to open a topic. Same rules as the refuse lab. Bad body → reject + audit line. Good body → create.
What it teaches: Self-service around Kafka. Teams should not need the raw CLI.

Title: Under-Replicated Report
What the shift is: Ship a command that lists partitions whose ISR is smaller than RF and exits non-zero when any exist. Healthy cluster → empty + exit 0.
What it teaches: On-call URP check is a tool.

Title: Lag Report for Dispatch
What the shift is: Ship a command that prints lag per rider.dispatch partition and exits non-zero over the ticket limit.
What it teaches: On-call lag check is a tool.

Title: One Key Owns the Topic
What the shift is: Almost all lag or produce load sits on one partition because a test producer used one key. Fix the keying / partitioner path in the ticket. Do not add brokers to hide skew.
What it teaches: Hot partition. Capacity is not the first lever.

Title: Move Replicas Onto the Empty Broker
What the shift is: A fourth broker is up and leads nothing. Reassign rider.dispatch onto it, wait for ISR, then spread preferred leadership. Do not leave preferred leaders piled on the old three.
What it teaches: New broker is unused until replicas move. Reassignment then preferred election.

Title: Shed Leadership Before the Patch
What the shift is: Take one broker out for a planned patch: shed leadership, keep produces succeeding under min.ISR=2, stop the broker, bring it back, wait for full ISR. An out-of-date broker must not become leader.
What it teaches: Planned drain / bounce. Same durability rules as incidents, without the fire.

Title: Leader Disk Full Desk Behind
What the shift is: Some rider.dispatch partitions reject writes; the desk is behind on those partitions. Leader disk is full. Free disk or fail over to a caught-up replica. Read forward. Leave min.ISR; no unclean election; no reset to latest.
What it teaches: Disk + stuck consume in one page.

Title: Offsets After the Firefight
What the shift is: Someone started restaurant-alerts from latest during the last incident. Input is still there. Stop the group, restore offsets from the ticket, start again. Not earliest.
What it teaches: Offset is read position. Latest skips backlog.

Title: Two Topics One Full Broker
What the shift is: ISR shrinks on the hot topic because a second topic filled the same broker's log dir. Fix both so the next wave does not repeat.
What it teaches: Shared-broker disk contention. Multi-signal diagnosis.

Title: Drain While the Cluster Is Already Hurting
What the shift is: A broker must leave for a failing disk, but shedding onto the remaining brokers recreates the earlier overcommit. Drain with writes still accepted under min.ISR=2; prove preferred placement still holds.
What it teaches: Decommission under pressure without making URP permanent.

Title: Quota Listener and Disk Together
What the shift is: A client quota starves the desk, advertised bootstrap is stale after a move, and one broker disk is full. Restore produce and consume without the three wrong shortcuts in the ticket.
What it teaches: Compound: clients + networking + node. Fix the system.

Title: First Shift on the Kafka Cluster
What the shift is: The cluster is already up. Record the controller, the leader of rider.dispatch partition 3, and how far that partition has been written. Delete leftover scratch. Leave orders, restaurant.notifications, and rider.dispatch alone.
What it teaches: Controller, partition leader, and log end.

Title: Open the Order Status Topic
What the shift is: Create order.status the QuickBite way: 6 partitions, RF=3, 3-day retention, min.ISR=2. Do not change the three topics already live.
What it teaches: Topic shape. Superseded in spirit by Foundations 1.2 with a new pack id when built.

Title: Orders-Audit Has One Copy
What the shift is: orders-audit has one copy per partition, all on kafka-0. Raise RF to 3 and wait for ISR. Keep current leaders.
What it teaches: Reassignment. Lesson DNA may feed Foundations or Capacity later.

Title: Broker 2 Left the ISR
What the shift is: kafka-2 stopped; URP on rider.dispatch. Start broker; wait for ISR=3; leave min.ISR=2.
What it teaches: Maps to Foundations 1.5 lesson DNA.

Title: Rider Dispatch Is Rejecting Writes
What the shift is: RF too low for min.ISR with a broker down. Restore RF and broker; leave min.ISR=2.
What it teaches: Maps to Foundations 1.6 lesson DNA.

Title: Disk Full on Broker 1
What the shift is: Log dir full from debug-dump + keep-forever. Free disk; leave hot path alone.
What it teaches: Maps to Foundations 1.7 lesson DNA.

Title: Orders Was Compacted
What the shift is: orders switched to compact; history gone. Put orders back to delete; compact belongs on the status changelog.
What it teaches: Compaction lesson folded into Foundations 1.7 when rebuilt.

Title: One Partition of Rider Dispatch Is Behind
What the shift is: One partition lag; wedged member. Restart instance; lag drains by reading.
What it teaches: Maps to Consumer Groups 2.2.

Title: Put the Notification Offsets Back
What the shift is: Group reset to latest; restore ticket offsets.
What it teaches: Maps to Consumer Groups 2.3.

Title: Rider Dispatch Incident
What the shift is: Disk full + stuck desk; no unclean election; no reset to latest.
What it teaches: Maps to Foundations 1.8 / Incidents 6.1.
